{{short description|Passwordless authentication credential key}}
{{About|passwordless authentication credential key|W3C standardisation for web authentication|WebAuthn|other methods of authentication used on the web|Authentication#In computer science}}

[[File:Bitwarden Passkey window screenshot.png|thumb|Login passkey selection page to application ([[Pixiv]]) through password manager ([[Bitwarden]])]]

'''Passkey'''<ref name="fido-passkey">{{cite web |title=FIDO Passkeys: Passwordless Authentication |url=https://fidoalliance.org/passkeys/ |website=FIDO Alliance |access-date=30 August 2026 |date=11 October 2024}}</ref><ref name="techrepublic">{{cite news |last1=Shein |first1=Esther |title=Apple touts Passkey, its new privacy feature, at WWDC 2022 |url=https://www.techrepublic.com/article/apple-touts-passkey-its-new-privacy-feature-at-wwdc-2022/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |work=TechRepublic |publisher=TechnologyAdvice |date=2022-06-06 |archive-date=2023-09-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230920063720/https://www.techrepublic.com/article/apple-touts-passkey-its-new-privacy-feature-at-wwdc-2022/ |url-status=live }}</ref>, also known as '''security key'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Register a passkey with a FIDO2 security key - Microsoft Entra ID |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-register-passkey-with-security-key |website=learn.microsoft.com |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=en-us}}</ref>, is a pair of [[cryptographic]] keys that is generated by a user's [[authenticator]] linked to an account to [[authentication|authenticate]] a user's identity against a remote application or system by using [[public-key cryptography]], thus avoiding the need to reveal the secret key held by the user through public channels.<ref name="mdn">{{cite web |title=Passkeys - Security |url=https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Authentication/Passkeys |website=MDN Web Docs |access-date=30 August 2026 |date=2 April 2026}}</ref><ref name="docsrs-webauthnrs">{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=William |title=webauthn-rs docs |url=https://docs.rs/webauthn-rs/latest/webauthn_rs/#what-is-a-passkey |website=Docs.rs |publisher=Kanidm Identity Management Project |access-date=3 July 2025 |date=April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250612151121/https://docs.rs/webauthn-rs/latest/webauthn_rs/#what-is-a-passkey |archive-date=12 June 2025}}</ref> The current popular implementation of passkeys for general public usage in [[web development|web technologies]] is proposed by [[FIDO Alliance]] and standardised by the [[World Wide Web Consortium]] under the [[WebAuthn]] standard<ref>{{cite web |title=White Paper: Multi-Device FIDO Credentials |url=https://fidoalliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/How-FIDO-Addresses-a-Full-Range-of-Use-Cases-March24.pdf |publisher=[[FIDO Alliance]] |access-date=20 May 2024 |page=6 |date=March 2022 |archive-date=16 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240616202812/https://fidoalliance.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/How-FIDO-Addresses-a-Full-Range-of-Use-Cases-March24.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://fidoalliance.org/overview/history/ | title=History of FIDO Alliance | date=22 December 2014 | access-date=30 August 2019 | archive-date=23 May 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230523182546/https://fidoalliance.org/overview/history/ | url-status=live }}</ref>, and passkeys is generally referred as a ''[[de-facto]]'' non-technical term of WebAuthn credential.<ref name="docsrs-webauthnrs" />

== Technical ==

Passkey is based on [[public-key cryptography]] that is designed for passwordless authentication, where user [[credential]] is a private key stored on the user's authenticator and the application system stores the public key that can be used to create a cryptographic challenge that can only be solved by the user credential, thereby authenticating the user's identity. The process transfers only publicly-known information to the user, who then returns the solved challenge without transferring the private key openly through public channels (which may be [[eavesdropping|eavesdropped]]), thus making it more secure than traditional authentication method such as [[passwords]] that could be tapped and used by remote attackers.<ref>{{cite web |title=What is a Passkey? Secure Signins |url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-my/security/business/security-101/what-is-passkey |website=Microsoft Security |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=en-MY}}</ref> The term ''passkey'' does not refer to any specific technology, but due to the origin and widespread adoption within FIDO2 ecosystem, the term is now commonly associated with FIDO2 credential.<ref name="fido-passkey">{{cite web |title=FIDO Passkeys: Passwordless Authentication |url=https://fidoalliance.org/passkeys/ |website=FIDO Alliance |access-date=30 August 2026 |date=11 October 2024}}</ref>

The user credential (private key) is stored inside an authenticator, which may be a physical device (common referred as a security key), [[secure cryptoprocessor]] such as [[Trusted Platform Module]], [[password managers]] or [[keyring (cryptography)|keyrings]]. Software-based authenticator clients may offer additional features such as [[biometric]] authentication like [[Touch ID]] or [[Windows Hello]] for better security, or cloud sync for ease of usage across devices.<ref name="docsrs-webauthnrs"/>

== Implementations ==

=== FIDO2 (WebAuthn + CTAP2) ===

{{main|WebAuthn|Client to Authenticator Protocol}}

FIDO2 passkeys are commonly used by [[web development|web technologies]] such as [[mobile apps]] and [[websites]] for user authentication. This is done by allowing applications to request a challenge from the device client (e.g. [[web browser]] or [[operating system]]) through [[WebAuthn]], and then the device client relaying to the hardware carrying out the cryptographic operation through [[Client to Authenticator Protocol|CTAP2]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Quick overview of WebAuthn FIDO2 and CTAP |url=https://developers.yubico.com/Passkeys/Quick_overview_of_WebAuthn_FIDO2_and_CTAP.html |website=developers.yubico.com |access-date=30 August 2026}}</ref>

The use of the term ''passkey'' to refer to the private key/user credential starts in June 2022, where [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] announces that they will start to support passkeys as an authentication method in [[iOS]] and [[macOS]] devices,<ref name="zdnet">{{cite news |last1=Clemons |first1=Taylor |title=WWDC 2022: Apple announces Passkey feature to eliminate passwords across platforms |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/wwdc-2022-apple-announces-passkey-feature/ |access-date=2023-04-27 |work=ZDNET |date=2022-06-06 |archive-date=2023-06-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606212207/https://www.zdnet.com/article/wwdc-2022-apple-announces-passkey-feature/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="techrepublic" /> debuting the term "passkey" to the general public.<ref name="verge">{{cite news |last1=Shakir |first1=Umar |title=Reminder: passkeys are not just from Apple |url=https://www.theverge.com/2022/8/5/23293643/apple-passkeys-fido-alliance-passwordless-google-microsoft |access-date=2023-04-27 |work=The Verge |publisher=Vox Media |date=2022-08-06 |archive-date=2023-09-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230924231545/https://www.theverge.com/2022/8/5/23293643/apple-passkeys-fido-alliance-passwordless-google-microsoft |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Google]] announces that [[Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[Google Chrome]] will support passkeys too on October 2022,<ref name="wired">{{cite news |last1=Nield |first1=David |title=How to Use Passkeys in Google Chrome and Android |url=https://www.wired.com/story/how-to-use-passkeys-google-chrome-android/ |access-date=2023-05-04 |work=WIRED |publisher=Condé Nast |date=2022-10-16 |archive-date=2023-10-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005163813/https://www.wired.com/story/how-to-use-passkeys-google-chrome-android/ |url-status=live }}</ref> followed by [[Microsoft]] on [[Windows 11]] at September 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://thehackernews.com/2023/09/microsoft-is-rolling-out-support-for.html?m=1 |title=存档副本 |access-date=2024-07-13 |archive-date=2024-07-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240713142115/https://thehackernews.com/2023/09/microsoft-is-rolling-out-support-for.html}}</ref>

Some implementations of WebAuthn passkeys allow storage of user identifiers inside the passkey itself, allowing users to directly authenticate as the defined identity instead of providing an identifier (such as email or username) separately. Other implementations of WebAuthn passkeys acts as part of [[multi-factor authentication]], requiring additional authentication methods like password or email verification to be used together.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sign in with passkeys in Microsoft Entra External ID |url=https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/customers/how-to-sign-in-with-passkey?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=Microsoft Entra External ID |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Resident Key ===

A resident key is a private credential that is specifically stored inside an external physical device that may be disconnected from the machine that validates the credential. This is used by [[OpenSSH]] protocol.<ref name="docsrs-webauthnrs"/><ref>{{cite web |title=What Is Resident Key? Definition & Examples |url=https://nhimg.org/glossary/resident-key/ |website=NHI Management Group |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=en}}</ref> In WebAuthn, it is called a ''discoverable credential''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Discoverable vs non-discoverable credentials |url=https://developers.yubico.com/Passkeys/Passkey_concepts/Discoverable_vs_non-discoverable_credentials.html |website=developers.yubico.com |access-date=30 August 2026}}</ref>

=== FIDO UAF ===

FIDO Universal Authentication Framework (UAF), along with FIDO U2F, are precursor designs of FIDO2, and influenced the design of FIDO2. FIDO UAF stores the private key directly on physical devices (commonly smartphones) instead of relying on external authenticator protocol such as CTAP. As the private key is bounded to the physical device, it could not be backed up or transferred to another device.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mobile Authentication (FIDO UAF) Example Apps |url=https://docs.nevis.net/authcloud/example-apps/mobile-authentication-example-apps?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=Nevis documentation |access-date=30 August 2026 |language=en |date=5 August 2026}}</ref> 

== Benefits ==

Passkeys are more convenient than traditional authentication methods and offer greater resistance to [[phishing]] attacks.<ref name="mdn"/><ref name="microsoft">{{cite web |title=Expansion of FIDO standard and new updates for Microsoft passwordless solutions |url=https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/microsoft-entra-azure-ad-blog/expansion-of-fido-standard-and-new-updates-for-microsoft/ba-p/3290633 |website=Tech Community |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230926203858/https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/microsoft-entra-azure-ad-blog/expansion-of-fido-standard-and-new-updates-for-microsoft/ba-p/3290633 |archive-date=2023-09-26 |access-date=2023-04-27 |publisher=Microsoft |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="zdnet" /> They are protected by the devices on which they are stored and often leverage biometric authentication as an additional layer of security, eliminating the need for users to remember passwords. Compared with related terms such as FIDO and WebAuthn, the term “passkey” is generally preferred in marketing because it is less likely to cause confusion and avoid pushing out [[jargon]].<ref name="verge" /> However, as of 2026, most platforms still offer other methods of authentication alongside passkeys, which may reduce the benefits of using passkeys.<ref name="arstechnica-not-usable">{{cite web |last1=Goodin |first1=Dan |title=Passkey technology is elegant, but it's most definitely not usable security |date=30 December 2024 |url=https://arstechnica.com/security/2024/12/passkey-technology-is-elegant-but-its-most-definitely-not-usable-security/ |publisher=Ars Technica |access-date=3 July 2025 |archive-date=3 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250703130434/https://arstechnica.com/security/2024/12/passkey-technology-is-elegant-but-its-most-definitely-not-usable-security/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== In the media ==
Passkeys (implemented through WebAuthn) has received mixed responses from the public:
* [[Troy Hunt]]: "Passkeys are one of the few security constructs that make your life easier, rather than harder."<ref name="troyhunt">{{Cite web |last=Hunt |first=Troy |date=2025-05-05 |title=Passkeys for Normal People |url=https://www.troyhunt.com/passkeys-for-normal-people/ |access-date=2025-08-13 |website=Troy Hunt |language=en |archive-date=13 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250513190543/https://www.troyhunt.com/passkeys-for-normal-people/ |url-status=live }}</ref> "That's a one-click sign-in, and clicking the purple button immediately grants me access to my account."<ref name="troyhunt"/>
* Dan Goodin: "Passkey technology is elegant, but it’s most definitely not usable security."<ref name="arstechnica-not-usable" />
* [[Bruce Davie]]: "...the implementation seems to have failed the 'make it easy for users' test, which in my view is the whole point of passkeys. I have been using [[public key cryptography]] for 30-plus years... If I find passkeys confusing to use, it doesn’t bode well for more typical users."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Davie |first=Bruce |date=2024-11-17 |title=Will passkeys ever replace passwords? Can they? |url=https://www.theregister.com/2024/11/17/passkeys_passwords/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725180037/https://www.theregister.com/2024/11/17/passkeys_passwords/ |archive-date=25 July 2025 |access-date=2025-08-13 |work=[[The Register]] |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>
